🚢Hormuz Vessel Crossing Update: Recovery Stalls at 19 — Tankers 10, Dry Cargo 9 Commercial vessel crossings through the Strait of Hormuz have slipped to 19 over the latest 24-hour rolling window — 10 tankers and 9 dry cargo ships — down from 24 yesterday and a full 67% below the June 24 recovery peak of 57. What looked like a rebuilding of traffic into late June has flattened into four straight readings stuck in the high-teens-to-20s, well short of anything resembling normal. Breaking it out by vessel type tells the story of the stall. Both segments spiked on June 24 — 24 tankers and 33 dry cargo ships, each the strongest single-day count since the late-February collapse. But the dry-bulk dash has unwound fastest, off 73% from that peak versus 58% for tankers. The result: tankers have quietly reclaimed the slim majority of the flow (roughly 53%), closer to their pre-conflict share, but on a fraction of the volume.
